title: The Design Review Order Most PMs Get Backwards
description:
Design reviews go wrong two ways: the PM rubber-stamps everything, or relitigates the problem statement at the mockup stage -- way too late, and it wastes the designer's work. This Short breaks down the fixed order that catches real gaps instead: problem fit, acceptance criteria, edge cases, scope creep -- taste last.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/product-manager-mastery-path/level-1/06-working-with-design-engineering/

#Shorts

beats.narration: Ever sat through a design review that turned into an argument about button colors? That's not feedback -- that's the review happening in the wrong order.

display.heading: The Design Review Everyone Gets Wrong

beats.narration: Most design reviews go wrong one of two ways -- the PM rubber-stamps everything with no real feedback, or relitigates the problem itself, which by now just wastes the designer's work.

display.heading: Running a good design review
display.subheading: PMs go wrong two ways: rubber-stamping everything, or relitigating the problem too late.

beats.narration: The fix: a fixed order. Does this solve the actual problem? Does it meet the acceptance criteria? What edge cases are missing -- empty states, errors, mobile? Is anything scope creep? Only then, talk taste.

display.heading: Review in this order
display.subheading: Problem fit, then acceptance criteria, then edge cases, then scope creep -- taste last.

beats.narration: That exact order is what caught a real gap once: a notifications mockup with no empty state for zero notifications -- found by asking the right question, not by taste.

display.heading: Worked example
display.subheading: A missing empty state, caught by the checklist -- not a preference.
